{{Short description|FIFA World Cup group}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=December 2025}}
{{Use American English|date=November 2025}}
Group A<!---Do not bold, per [[MOS:TITLEABSENTBOLD]]. See also previous FIFA World Cup group pages, which do not bold the group---> of the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]] took place from June 11 to 24, 2026.<ref name="match schedule">{{cite web |url=https://digitalhub.fifa.com/m/1be9ce37eb98fcc5/original/FWC26-Match-Schedule_English.pdf |title=FIFA World Cup 26 – Match Schedule |publisher=[[FIFA]] |date=February 4, 2024 |access-date=February 4, 2024}}</ref> The group consisted of national football teams representing [[Mexico national football team|Mexico]] (co-host), [[South Africa national soccer team|South Africa]], [[South Korea national football team|South Korea]], and the [[Czech Republic national football team|Czech Republic]]. This also marked the return of the Czech Republic and South Africa to the World Cup, respectively, since [[2006 FIFA World Cup|2006]] and [[2010 FIFA World Cup|2010]]. 

The top two teams, Mexico and South Africa, secured their place in the [[2026 FIFA World Cup knockout stage#Round of 32|round of 32]]. Mexico won the group, winning three consecutive games, while South Africa won one game and drew the other, having lost their opening match to Mexico. South Korea finished third, having won one game, while the Czech Republic finished fourth with a single point.

==Matches==
All times listed are local.<ref name="match schedule"/>

===Mexico vs South Africa===
[[File:BUENOS DÍAS, MÉXICO ASÍ DESPIERTA EL ESTADIO CIUDAD DE MÉXICO PARA EL MUNDIAL (7).jpg|thumb|right|Inside Estadio Azteca prior to the opening match]]

The two teams had faced each other four times, most recently in a [[2010 FIFA World Cup Group A#South Africa vs Mexico|1–1]] draw in the [[2010 FIFA World Cup]] [[List of FIFA World Cup opening matches|opening match]], with South Africa as the host nation.<ref>{{cite web|title=Mexico national football team: record v South Africa |url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/mexico/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/South%20Africa|website=11v11.com|access-date=December 5, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Mexico vs. South Africa Head-to-Head in the World Cups|url=https://www.thesoccerworldcups.com/head_to_head/mexico_vs_south_africa.php|website=thesoccerworldcups.com|access-date=December 5, 2025}}</ref> This match coincidentally took place exactly 16 years after. Additionally, South Africa manager [[Hugo Broos]] and Mexico’s [[Javier Aguirre]] encountered each other on the same pitch during the [[1986 FIFA World Cup|1986 World Cup]] as players for [[Belgium national football team|Belgium]] and Mexico, respectively.

Mexico went in front in the 9th minute when [[Julián Quiñones]] scored with a low right footed finish through the legs of South African goalkeeper [[Ronwen Williams]] from just inside the penalty area after [[Sphephelo Sithole]] was caught in possession on the edge of the penalty area by [[Erik Lira]]. Four minutes into the second half, South Africa's Sphephelo Sithole was sent-off after fouling Mexico's [[Brian Gutiérrez]] when he was going through on goal.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c0myn4dwvzkt|title= Mexico 2 South Africa 0|date=12 June 2026|work=BBC Sport|accessdate=13 June 2026}}</ref>
It was 2–0 in the 67th minute when [[Raúl Jiménez]] scored his first goal at a World Cup finals, a header at the back post to the left of the net after a cross from the right by [[Roberto Alvarado]].

In the 73rd minute, South African substitute [[Themba Zwane]] was sent off for a slap in the face of Mexican forward Roberto Alvarado. In the 92nd minute there was a third [[List of FIFA World Cup red cards|red card]] in the game with Mexican captain [[César Montes]] sent off for denying a goalscoring opportunity by fouling [[Khuliso Mudau]] with Mexico going on to win the game 2–0.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/11/mexico-south-africa-world-cup-2026-group-a-match-report|title= Raúl Jiménez seals Mexico's win against nine-man South Africa in World Cup opener|date=12 June 2026|work=Guardian|accessdate=13 June 2026}}</ref>

This marked the first time Mexico won an opening match as they had lost opening matches in [[1930 World Cup|1930]], [[1950 FIFA World Cup|1950]] and [[1954 FIFA World Cup|1954]], and drawing in the [[1970 FIFA World Cup|1970]] (as hosts) and [[2010 FIFA World Cup|2010]] editions.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.thehindu.com/sport/football/fifa-world-cup-mexico-wins-opening-game-for-the-first-time/article71092175.ece|title= FIFA World Cup: Mexico wins opening game for the first time|date= 12 June 2026|work=[[The Hindu]]|accessdate= 9 July 2026}}</ref> This marked the first opening match with the most red cards in [[FIFA World Cup]] history. It also has the most red cards since the [[Battle of Nuremberg (2006 FIFA World Cup)|Battle of Nuremberg]], which was a match between Portugal vs Netherlands in the [[2006 FIFA World Cup]] that had a total of 4 red cards.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Raghuraman |first=Anantaajith |date=2026-06-25 |title=Breaking down the dirtiest World Cup opening game we’ve ever seen – or was it? |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7352942/2026/06/11/world-cup-mexico-south-africa-red-cards/ |access-date=2026-10-07 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

===South Korea vs Czech Republic===
[[File:South Corea-Czechia2026FWC.jpg|thumb|Pre-match ceremony between South Korea and Czech Republic]]
The teams had played each other three times, most recently in a 2016 friendly, a 2–1 victory for the South Koreans.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/czech-republic/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/Korea+Republic/|title=Czech Republic national football team: record v Korea Republic|website=www.11v11.com}}</ref> South Korea and [[Czechoslovakia national football team|Czechoslovakia]], the Czech Republic's predecessor state, met previously three times in the 1980s, with a win for the Koreans and two draws.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/korea-republic/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/Czechoslovakia/|title=Korea Republic national football team: record v Czechoslovakia|website=www.11v11.com}}</ref> The fixture marked the Czech Republic's return to the World Cup after a 20-year absence, following a group-stage elimination in [[2006 FIFA World Cup|2006]] during their debut as an independent nation.

The Czech Republic went in front in the 59th minute with a header from captain [[Ladislav Krejčí (footballer, born 1999)|Ladislav Krejčí]] to the right of the net from six yards out after a long throw-in from [[Vladimir Coufal]] from the right. It was 1–1 in the 67th minute when [[Hwang In-beom]] received the ball from [[Lee Kang-in]] before turning back onto his right foot before scooping the ball over the advancing [[Matěj Kovář]] and into the right of the net.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/12/south-korea-czechia-world-cup-2026-group-a-match-report|title= South Korea get off to winning start after rallying from goal down to beat Czechia|date=12 June 2026|work=Guardian|accessdate=13 June 2026}}</ref>

In the 78th minute, [[Tomáš Souček]] headed in a free kick from the left, but the goal was ruled out for offside. In the 80th minute, [[Hwang In-beom]] crossed low from the right and [[Oh Hyeon-gyu]] finished from six yards out to the left of the net to put South Korea 2–1 in front. In the 82nd minute, South Korean goalkeeper [[Kim Seung-gyu]] saved down low to his right to stop [[Adam Hložek]]'s close-range effort with South Korea going on to win 2–1.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/ckg0vvrg70vt|title= South Korea 2 Czech Republic 1|date=12 June 2026|work=BBC Sport|accessdate=13 June 2026}}</ref>

===Czech Republic vs South Africa===
The teams had only played each other in the [[1997 FIFA Confederations Cup]], where the teams drew [[1997 FIFA Confederations Cup Group B#South Africa v Czech Republic|2–2]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/czech-republic/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/South+Africa/|title=Czech Republic national football team: record v South Africa|website=www.11v11.com}}</ref> This was the only match in Group A held outside of Mexico.

By officiating this match, referees [[Tori Penso]], [[Brooke Mayo]], and [[Kathryn Nesbitt]] became the second all-female on-field refereeing trio, and the first from the United States, to take charge of a match at a men's FIFA World Cup.<ref>{{cite web |title=All-Woman Referee Trio Takes Center Stage at FIFA World Cup 2026 |url=https://ussoccer.com |website=U.S. Soccer |date=June 17, 2026 |access-date=June 30, 2026}}</ref>

In the 6th minute, [[Michal Sadílek]] scored with a finish from the left of the penalty area into the right of the net. In the 83rd minute, South Africa were awarded a penalty when a shot from [[Thapelo Maseko]] hit the arm of [[Pavel Šulc]] inside the penalty area. [[Teboho Mokoena (soccer, born 1997)|Teboho Mokoena]] scored the penalty, sending the goalkeeper the wrong way with a shot to the left to make it 1–1.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cp8rk9gwzjnt|title= Czech Republic 1 South Africa 1|date=18 June 2026|work=BBC Sport |accessdate=19 June 2026}}</ref>

===Mexico vs South Korea===
The sides have previously met 15 times including twice in the World Cup, with Mexico winning both matches: [[1998 FIFA World Cup Group E#South Korea vs Mexico|3–1]] in the [[1998 FIFA World Cup|1998 tournament]] in France, and [[2018 FIFA World Cup Group F#South Korea vs Mexico|2–1]] in the [[2018 FIFA World Cup|2018 edition]] in Russia. Their most recent meeting was a 2–2 draw in 2025.<ref>{{cite web|title=Mexico national football team: record v South Korea|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/mexico/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/Korea%20Republic|website=11v11.com|access-date=December 5, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Mexico vs. South Korea Head-to-Head in the World Cups|url=https://www.thesoccerworldcups.com/head_to_head/mexico_vs_south_korea.php|website=thesoccerworldcups.com|access-date=December 5, 2025}}</ref>

In the 50th minute, South Korean goalkeeper [[Kim Seung-gyu]] spilled the ball after a collision with his own player, [[Lee Gi-hyuk]]. The ball fell to Mexico's [[Luis Romo]] allowing him to hook it back into an empty net.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cvgme6np19pt|title= Mexico 1 South Korea 0|date=18 June 2026|work=BBC Sport |accessdate=19 June 2026}}</ref>

With the 1–0 win, Mexico became the first team to qualify for the newly introduced round of 32.

===Czech Republic vs Mexico===
The teams only played each other once in 2000, a 2–1 win for the Czechs.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/czech-republic/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/Mexico/|title=Czech Republic national football team: record v Mexico|website=www.11v11.com}}</ref> Czechoslovakia played Mexico at the [[1962 FIFA World Cup]] in a match in which Czechoslovakia scored after just 15 seconds, the second-fastest goal in World Cup history. However, Mexico came back to win [[1962 FIFA World Cup Group 3#Mexico vs Czechoslovakia|3–1]]. Their other two meetings saw both teams win once in friendlies.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.11v11.com/teams/mexico/tab/opposingTeams/opposition/Czechoslovakia/|title=Mexico national football team: record v Czechoslovakia|website=www.11v11.com}}</ref>

By defeating the Czech Republic 3–0, Mexico won all three World Cup group stage matches for the first time in its history. This achievement left Mexico as the only co-host to secure a perfect group stage record, following Canada's [[2026 FIFA World Cup Group B#Switzerland vs Canada|2–1 loss]] to [[Switzerland national football team|Switzerland]] and the United States [[2026 FIFA World Cup Group D#Turkey vs United States|3–2 defeat]] against [[Turkey national football team|Turkey]]. Additionally, they were one of only three teams in the tournament to achieve a perfect nine-point streak, alongside [[France national football team|France]] and defending champions [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]].<ref>{{Cite tweet |user=TheAthleticFC |number=2069978536270586027 |title=Mexico win all three group stage matches at a men's World Cup for the first time in their history. Goals from Mateo Chavez, Julian Quinones and Alvaro Fidalgo earn a comfortable victory for their country against the Czech Republic, who leave the tournament with a whimper. Mexico signed off the victory with the introduction of Guillermo Ochoa, who appeared for what could be his last World Cup match at the age of 40.}}</ref> Czechia were eliminated from the tournament after losing their second group game, and South Africa defeated South Korea to claim second place in the group.

Additionally, [[Guillermo Ochoa]] secured his sixth FIFA World Cup squad selection, joining [[Lionel Messi]] of Argentina and [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] of Portugal in achieving this historic milestone.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Wilson |first=Chris |date=25 June 2026 |title=Mexico legend Guillermo Ochoa joins Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo in exclusive World Cup club |url=https://www.the-independent.com/sport/football/guillermo-ochoa-mexico-world-cup-czech-republic-messi-ronaldo-b3002625.html |work=[[The Independent]]}}</ref>

===South Africa vs South Korea===
[[File:South Korea and South Africa flags before their game at World Cup 2026.jpg|thumb|right|Pre-match ceremony between South Africa and South Korea]]
The two teams had never met before.

In the 63rd minute, [[Thapelo Maseko]] received the ball on the right before shooting left-footed low into the right corner of the net from twelve yards out.

With a 1–0 victory, South Africa qualified for the knockout stages of a World Cup for the first time, as runners-up of Group A, while South Korea finished in third and was ultimately eliminated from the group stage as a result of their third-place ranking dropping down after other group results were finalized.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cy9rxgz1551t|title=South Africa 1 South Korea 0|date=24 June 2026|work=BBC Sport|accessdate=25 June 2026}}</ref>

South Korea's exit from the tournament prompted head coach [[Hong Myung-bo]] to resign on June 28, amid fierce public backlash that included sharp condemnation from President [[Lee Jae-myung]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=South Korea coach Hong Myung-Bo quits after World Cup exit, criticism from president |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/49208667/south-korea-coach-hong-myung-bo-quits-world-cup-exit-criticism-president |access-date=2026-06-28 |publisher=ESPN}}</ref> His lack of tactical flexibility shocked South Korean media and fans, and he was strongly criticized for overseeing a group-stage elimination at the World Cup for the second time, following [[2014 FIFA World Cup Group H|his previous failure]] in [[2014 FIFA World Cup|2014]] after losses against Algeria and Belgium.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.chosun.com/english/sports-en/2026/06/26/DWPMD3A6EZDCBNF2RGTQUELWBY/ |title=Hong Myung-bo's Stubborn Tactics Lead to World Cup Defeat, Echoing 2014 Mistakes |publisher=The Chosun Ilbo |date=2026-06-26 |access-date=2026-06-28}}</ref>

==Discipline==
The team conduct ("fair play") score would have been used as a tiebreaker if the head-to-head and overall records of teams were tied. It would also be used as a tiebreaker for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup#Ranking of third-place teams|third-place ranking]] between groups if the overall records of teams were tied. The score was calculated based on yellow and red cards received by players and team officials in all group matches as follows:<ref name="regulations"/>
*yellow card: −1 point;
*indirect red card (second yellow card): −3 points;
*direct red card: −4 points;
*yellow card and direct red card: −5 points;

Only one of the above deductions could be applied to a player or team official in a single match.
